expect: Up to 4 marks for two developed points. Strength: official statistics from the Department for Education are large-scale, covering all schools in England, and longitudinal — allowing researchers to track trends in achievement by class, gender and ethnicity over many years (as Halsey did). This gives high reliability: the same data can be checked and compared by other researchers. Weakness: official statistics are socially constructed — they reflect decisions about what to measure. League table positions measure exam results but not the value added to pupils' progress. A school with a disadvantaged intake scoring below the national average may be more effective than a school in a wealthy area scoring higher, but the statistics do not capture this.
